summary.value: The Naked Neck, often called the Turken or Transylvanian Naked Neck, is a chicken with a bare band of red skin from the shoulders to the head. It is all chicken; the old idea that it is a turkey cross is a myth. One dominant gene causes the bare neck, and the bird has only about half the usual number of feathers. Its recorded history centers on Transylvania in Romania, and Germany later refined it. The APA accepts black, white, buff and red. Cocks weigh about 8.5 pounds and hens about 6.5. Hens lay light brown eggs of medium size at a fair rate. The breed is kept for both eggs and meat, since the carcass is meaty and quick to pluck. Turkens are calm, friendly and easy to tame, forage well and handle cold better than their looks suggest.
